902-about-the-desautels-faculty-of-manag: A very international business school with students and professors from every continent and a focus on global issues. Internships and exchanges in Europe, Asia, the US and South America.
902-about-the-bachelor-of-commerce-bcom-: Prepares you for professional and managerial careers through critical thinking, integrating disciplines, applying theory, teamwork and leadership. A broad core gives quantitative, analytical and communication skills; specializations add depth.

General Management: focus on at least two areas, one Management concentration plus a second concentration or an outside minor. Suits a broad business education, later study such as law or industrial relations, or careers across sectors.
Majors and honours focus on one area, for clear goals or designations such as CPA or CFA.

International Management: the International Business Concentration, an outside Minor, a language to intermediate level, and international learning through exchange, study away or a study trip; credits vary by courses taken abroad.
Honours in Investment Management combines rigorous study with real investing, global internships and corporate partners.
902-administrative-officers: Yolande Chan, Dean. Benjamin Croitoru, Associate Dean, Undergraduate Programs. Heather McCombie, Associate Director, BCom Program. Jennifer Hunter, Associate Director, Student Affairs.
902-location: BCom Student Affairs Office, for all students in undergraduate Management courses: Samuel Bronfman Building, Room 228, 1001 Sherbrooke St. W., H3A 1G5; 514-398-4068; mcgill.ca/desautels/programs/bcom.
902-b-com-degree-requirements: 120 credits full-time over three or four years; generally 90 with Advanced Standing or a Quebec CEGEP diploma. Those from outside Quebec without an equivalent need 120.
Everyone needs a 3-credit experiential learning course. Teaching is in English, but you may submit work and write exams in French, which matters for business in Quebec.
903-absence-policy: Attend regularly and tell your instructor promptly about absences and why. No documents needed for illness under five days. A medical note may be requested after five consecutive days if you miss a required activity or assessment. Missing over 20% of a course may be impossible to accommodate; withdrawal may be best. For repeated trouble contact bcom.mgmt@mcgill.ca.

Non-medical absences like varsity events may need documents. You make up missed learning. For a missed assessment with a valid reason, ask your instructor, who follows PASL article 7 and judges what's fair and workable. Instructors are encouraged to plan flexible assessments.
903-academic-advising: The BCom Student Affairs Office advises all year on your degree, courses and policies, but you lead your own planning and are responsible for meeting requirements and deadlines.

Review your unofficial transcript and myProgress regularly, though myProgress can make mistakes, so check against the catalogue and Areas of Study page. Verify registration before add/drop ends. A graduation check before your final term is required.

Math and Statistics or Economics majors also see a departmental advisor. Minors need departmental advising and an approval form signed for the BCom office. Career Coaches are on the 6th floor of Bronfman.
903-when-to-contact-an-academic-advisor: For requirements, planning, registration, myProgress questions, changing programs, exams, summer courses, transfer credits, exchange, IUT, internships, leave, personal difficulties, long absences, policies, Academic Standing, the experiential requirement, and graduation.
They also help students elsewhere in Joint Honours Economics or the Minors in Management and Entrepreneurship, and prospective students; admissions questions go to Service Point.
See the BCom office site, the catalogue, or the BCom Hub in myCourses. Appointments in person or virtual through BCom Insight. A Local Wellness Advisor and the Wellness Hub also help.
Every new student must meet an advisor between October and the end of the first term, by email or booking form.
904-academic-requirements-for-graduation: Staff advise, but you are fully responsible for course choices, requirements, rules and deadlines. Misunderstanding won't earn an exception.
120 credits; a Quebec CEGEP diploma gives 30 of Advanced Standing, for 90. Others without an equivalent need 120. New students should verify transfer credits with an advisor.
904-students-entering-with-advanced-stan: Meet an advisor and get official results in by the end of your first term, or the credit may be denied. Deviating from your program needs the Associate Director's written permission. Transfers from other universities need at least 60 credits in the BCom.
904-experiential-learning-degree-require: At least 3 credits for those admitted from Fall 2024. Majors in Business Analytics, Managing for Sustainability or Retail Management and Honours in Investment Management can meet it through their program; check the course repository. Others use an elective or complementary. Not all run each term, so plan ahead.
905-academic-standing: Based mainly on CGPA, and sometimes TGPA. Assessed in January for Fall, May for Winter, and September for Summer; it decides if and how you continue. Fall results are "Interim", since deferred exams and two-term courses aren't counted yet. If not Satisfactory, see an advisor before withdrawal deadlines.
905-satisfactory-interim-satisfactory-st: CGPA of 2.00 or more; new students start here. You continue, and you need a 2.00 CGPA to graduate.
905-probationary-interim-probationary-st: You continue at a maximum of 14 credits a term, raise your GPA, and must see an advisor. Interim Probationary: review your load and strongly consider advice before Winter.

From Satisfactory: CGPA 1.50–1.99. Staying on Probation: CGPA 1.50–1.99 and TGPA 2.50+ (no TGPA test for Summer). From Interim Unsatisfactory: same CGPA and TGPA. Readmitted from Unsatisfactory: CGPA under 2.00, and meet your letter's conditions.
905-unsatisfactory-readmitted-standing: Applies after being readmitted from Unsatisfactory. Your letter sets your load and conditions; see an advisor.
905-unsatisfactory-interim-unsatisfactor: Interim: you may continue but must see an advisor before Winter withdrawal deadlines. Unsatisfactory: you can't continue, and your registration is cancelled.
Appeal in Minerva by July 15 (Fall) or November 15 (Winter), with proof of extenuating circumstances and reassurance of improvement. A second time means permanent withdrawal.
Triggers: CGPA below 1.50; or, from Probationary, Unsatisfactory Readmitted or Interim Unsatisfactory, TGPA below 2.50 with CGPA below 2.00.
905-incomplete-standings: Standing awaits deferred exam, or Standing Incomplete. From Winter or Summer you may register for Fall, but it must be resolved by add/drop's end. Unsatisfactory then cancels registration; see your advisor at once, as readmission needs proof and reassurance.
906-transfer-credit-and-advanced-standin: Up to 30 credits of Advanced Standing for good results in the DCS, IB, French or European Baccalaureate, Bologna countries, A and AS Levels, or AP. Transfers may cover up to a third of your degree, including program requirements.

See p. 55 for grades. P or S transfer only from McGill faculties. Letter grades from the other school take precedence. Get approval before exchange or study away. Residency: 80 credits for four-year, 60 for three-year. At most 6 online credits with department approval.
906-course-overlap: No credit for content overlapping McGill, CEGEP or other university courses, AP, A Levels, IB or French Baccalaureate. Ask the office and read exclusions.

Statistics: use the courses in Core and your program; others are judged case by case. Take them in order: MGCR 271 and MGSC 372 before MATH 324, never after. MATH 203, 204, PSYC 204 and 305 aren't open. Transferring from another faculty, McGill's MATH 203 exempts MGCR 271, but a pre-McGill MATH 203 doesn't.
Economics: at most 6 credits of Foundation courses; 9 among ECON 230D1/D2, 250D1/D2 and MGCR 293; 9 among ECON 332, 333, 295 and MGCR 294. ECON 208 and 209 aren't allowed; ECON 230D1/D2 isn't for U0.
The BCom is full-time, with part-time only for an occasional term in unusual circumstances.
906-course-requirements: C or better in all required and complementary courses, including Foundation. Repeat a failed required course, normally once; failure means below C, or J or KF. Substitutions only in special cases.

A failed complementary can be repeated or replaced; a replaced D stays as an elective credit. A repeated required D gives credit once. Both Ds count in your CGPA. Repeating a course you passed with C or better earns no credit and no CGPA effect.
907-courses-taken-under-the-satisfactory: Electives only, one per term, up to 10% of your McGill credits, chosen or cancelled by add/drop's end. S/U isn't in your GPA. Scholarships require 27 graded credits a year excluding Summer, so ask before using it. See p. 36.
907-cumulative-grade-point-average-cgpa: Graduate after your minimum credits and curriculum with a CGPA of 2.00, or 3.00 for Honours.
907-non-management-electives: Taking electives outside Desautels is strongly encouraged; Arts and Science are typically fine. Check eligibility in Minerva and the Restricted Electives page before add/drop ends. 100–200 level is suggested. Desautels courses can also serve.
Some faculties won't block you despite missing prerequisites, so check. Some departments such as Psychology reserve seats, so open spots may not be available.

Categories, subject to availability: AFRI, ANTH, ARTH, ATOC, BIOL, CANS, CATH, CHEM, CLAS, COMS, COMP, EAST, EPSC, ECON, ED (restricted), ENGL, ENVR, FREN, FRSL, GSFS, GEOG, HIST, INDG, INTD, ISLA, JWST, GERM, HISP, ITAL, LLCU, RUSS, LING, MATH, MUAR, MUTH, MUPD, MUHL (restricted), PHIL, PHYS, POLI, PSYC, PPOL, QCST, RELG, SOCI, WCOM (restricted).
907-registration: Register on time; space is limited. Returning students' priority for Fall and Winter starts in the last week of May; Summer Management courses open in early March.

If you can't get a course you need, send a Closed Course Request Form right after registering; waiting until add/drop can delay graduation. Continuing Studies courses don't count. Check credit and overlaps yourself: being let in by Minerva doesn't guarantee credit.
New students pick their specialization in Minerva first or get blocked; this can change later. Major and Concentration Fair for U1 each March. Watch BCom Hub alerts.

Changes in add/drop go through Minerva. Later withdrawals before the deadline give a W, with no GPA effect; after it, only in exceptional cases, starting with an advisor, and with substantial documents. Courses breaking rules get flagged not for credit.

New students: most decisions come by end of May, with registration in early to mid-June. Attend a virtual session in early June and in-person orientation. Advising runs May to classes by booking form. Use your McGill email from the moment you accept.
908-advising-schedules: Drop-in during add/drop and peak times for registration topics. 30-minute appointments after add/drop. An information session is required before exchange advising.
908-time-and-credit-limit-for-completion: With 90 or fewer credits to do, finish within eight terms of first registering; with over 90, this applies from a year after first registering. After a year or more away, request readmission in Minerva and in writing to bcom.mgmt@mcgill.ca; current requirements usually apply.
908-bcom-degree-admission-requirements: Highly selective, and minimums don't guarantee a place. See the admissions guide. Those required to withdraw elsewhere for poor grades can't transfer in. The office has interfaculty transfer details.
909-location: Samuel Bronfman Building, Room 228, 1001 Sherbrooke St. W., H3A 1G5; 514-398-4068; bcom.mgmt@mcgill.ca.
909-about-bcom-student-affairs-office: Advice on programs, requirements, registration, withdrawals, exams, rereads, Academic Standing, transfers, exchanges, scholarships, graduation and experiential learning, plus help through personal, financial or medical trouble. Immigration questions go to International Student Services or Service Point. Book through BCom Insight, or visit Room 228 if you can't.
909-grading-and-credit: In week one each instructor gives a written outline with topics, readings, office hours and contact details.
909-policy-on-assessment-of-student-lear: From PASL. The outline lists each assessment's due date, weight, structure, late penalties and delivery. Optional alternatives must be clear and open to all. If assessment changes after add/drop, you can choose original or new by a set date.

All due before the last exam day. No in-term tasks due in the last 10 working days of classes, except language orals, take-homes given at least 15 working days before classes end, and tasks worth 10% or less.
909-academic-integrity: Know what counts as cheating and plagiarism under the Code. New undergraduates complete the Academic Integrity tutorial in Minerva.
909-honours-and-first-class-honours: Honours: CGPA and program GPA of 3.0+. First-Class: both 3.5+. If below 3.0 or missing requirements, ask your advisor about graduating in another program.
910-graduation-scholarships-prizes-and-a: Merit-only awards are automatic for Fall or Winter graduates before Spring Convocation.

Apply online by early May: Anil Gondi Community Impact Award; B.Com. Class of 1986 Activity Award for Leadership; B.Com. Class of 1990 Activity Award; Jaclyn Lea Fisher Volunteer Leadership Award; Richard G. Donovan Prize in Case Excellence; Stephen S. Goldbloom Memorial Prize.

No application: Barry Clamen Prize; Cissy and Jimmy Greer Prize; Commerce 1925 Award; Dr. J. A. Coote Prize; Dr. M. Richard Gelfand Prize; Finestone Economics Prize; Herbert E. Siblin Award; Hugh Howson Memorial Prize; L. J. Forget and Company Awards; Laddie Millen Memorial Prizes; McGill Accounting Society Prize; McGill Alumnae Society Prize; Misawa Homes Prize; Peter S. Wise Memorial Prize; Sir Edward Beatty Medal.
910-in-course-scholarships-prizes-and-aw: Requires 27 graded credits in fall and winter, or 14 in one term. Merit-only awards are automatic; those mixing academics, volunteering and leadership need one online application by early June.

Application needed: Commerce 1955, Danny and Monica Gold, Devon Anthony Haye, Donald R. McRobie, Dr. Alex Paterson, Great-West Life and London Life, Hazelview, HSBC, Marcel A. Desautels, Marion McCall Daly, Paul-Hervé Desrosiers, Peter Brojde, Sheila Wellington BMO, Shirin Yeganegi, Anil Gondi (every three years), Philippe and Nan-B de Gaspé Beaubien (odd years).

Automatic: Accenture, André Desmarais and Francine Chrétien-Desmarais, Barry Clamen, Cecil Vineberg, Commerce 1953, Deloitte, Dorothy Esmé Graham Snell, Elizabeth Macfarlane, Frederick M. Connell, Gary and Wendy Balter, George Arnold Hart, Gerald Benjamin Wasserman, Jon Hartwick, John V. Galley, Joseph H. Jacobs, Letko Brosseau, McGill Alumnae Helen R. Y. Reid, Richter, Robert Bruce, Sir William Macdonald, Sujata Madan, Women Associates of McGill. The Dobson Centre awards the Dobson Cup Grit Prize and Peter Johnson Start-Up Prize.

You must be full-time in the BCom the next fall and winter, or full-time at McGill while not on exchange. Summer or Fall graduates can't get these but can apply for graduating awards. Awards are revoked if you stop qualifying, and aren't kept while you're on leave.
911-examinations: See p. 62. Enrolment Services posts schedules around early November and March and seating late in the last week of classes, and emails you about conflicts. Don't book travel before the schedule is out. A D or F means retaking core and program courses, though D passes for electives.
911-supplemental-examinations: None in undergraduate Desautels courses. To improve, repeat the course in a later term; extra work isn't allowed.
911-deferred-examinations: Never arrange a makeup with your professor. If illness or another serious reason stops you, apply in Minerva; documents may be needed, dated within 5 days of the exam, sent to the office quickly. If approved, write in the official period: March for Fall, August for Winter and Summer. Check the schedule yourself and see an advisor.
911-verification-of-grades-and-rereads: Under the Charter you may see any marked work and discuss it. If you suspect a final grade error, submit a Re-Read Application Form; during term, go to the instructor first.
Two types: coursework and final exams. Reviewers judge whether the original grade was fair, not regrade from scratch. A new grade replaces the old, higher or lower.
911-reread-of-coursework: Apply within 10 working days of getting work back; it's usually done within 20. Group work needs everyone's consent, with one fee. Talk to the instructor first.
911-rereads-of-final-exams: Apply in writing by March 31 for Fall and September 30 for Winter or Summer, strictly. Talking to the instructor is recommended. Courses from other faculties follow those faculties' rules.
911-international-exchange-program: Over 60 business schools worldwide. Requires a CGPA of 3.0, and at least two-thirds of departmental requirements done at McGill.

After nomination, check courses in the Course Equivalency Database and get transfer approval for all courses, electives included, with the TCAF in Minerva before classes start abroad. Letter grades only, no pass-fail; no credit for overlaps. Outside-program courses need departmental approval. Complete the Travel Registry or risk cancellation, and have your final transcript sent. Questions: 514-398-4068, bcom.mgmt@mcgill.ca.
912-bcom-programs-offered: Several B.Com. programs, in the categories below.
912-foundation-program-course-distributi: For 97–120 credit programs: 30 credits in year one, with MATH 122, MATH 123, MGCR 233, MGCR 250 and electives.
912-u0-elective-courses: Non-Management restrictions apply. C minimum in all U0 courses. Up to 6 elective credits may be replaced by listed core courses if space allows.
912-two-concentrations: 90 credits: Core 42, two concentrations 30, electives 18. 120 credits: add Foundation 30.
913-one-concentration-and-one-minor-18-o: 90 credits: Core 42, concentration 15, minor 18 or 24, electives 15 or 9. 120 credits: add Foundation 30. At least 18 minor credits must not overlap elsewhere.
913-concentrations: Accounting; Business Analytics; Entrepreneurship; Ethics; Finance; Information Technology Management; International Business; Labour-Management Relations and Human Resources; Managing for Sustainability; Marketing; Operations Management; Organizational Behaviour; Retail Management; Strategic Management (Global Strategy; Social Business & Enterprise).
913-minors-minor-concentrations-for-mana: Many in Arts and Science, often Anthropology, Canadian Studies, Computer Science, English Literature, Environmental Studies, Geological Sciences, German, History, International Development, Political Science and Women's Studies. The 3-credit experiential course is still required.
913-bcom-program-credit-structure-major-: Under review; may be updated before Fall 2026.
913-majors-in-management: 90 credits: Core 42, Major 30, electives 18. 120 credits: add Foundation 30.
913-major-in-mathematics-and-statistics-: 90 credits: Core 42, Major 30–33, electives 18 or 15. 120 credits: Math Foundation 10 (MATH 140, 141, 133; not for CEGEP students), Foundation 17, Core 42, Major 30–33, electives 21 or 18.
913-major-in-economics-for-management-st: 90 credits: Core 33, Major 36, electives 21. 120 credits: Foundation 18, Core 33, Major 36, electives 33. MGCR 271 counts toward the Major; ECON courses exempt MGCR 293 and 294.
914-major-in-international-management: Under review; may be updated before Fall 2026. 90 credits: Core 42, International Business 15, Minor Concentration 18, Language 9–12, Experiential 0–3, electives 0–6. 120 credits: Foundation 27 and electives 3–9. Exchange gives credit for approved courses, not 3 extra.
914-major-in-managing-for-sustainability: 90 credits: Core 42, Major 30, electives 18. 120 credits: Foundation 18, Core 42, Major 30, electives 30.
914-honours-in-investment-management: 90 credits: Core 42, Honours 45, electives 3. 120 credits: Foundation 27, Core 42, Honours 45, electives 6.
914-management-core: 42 credits for all, unless a major or honours changes it. C or better; repeat a D.
914-core-course-distribution: Admitted before Fall 2024: 39 credits of Core.
914-required-courses-42-credits: Admitted before Fall 2024: no MGCR 233, 39 credits; check MyProgress. ECON 295 taken before Fall 2024 with C or higher replaces MGCR 294.
Economics majors replace MGCR 293 with ECON 230D1/D2, and MGCR 294 with ECON 332 and 333 in second year.
915-concentrations-general-management-st: C or better in all concentration courses; below that, repeat, replace, or switch. Usually starts in U2. Each has an academic mentor, listed on the BCom site. A second concentration needs 15 non-overlapping credits at C or better.
915-program-description: For those who want to understand and use financial information, not become accountants. Part of General Management, with courses serving other programs too.
916-program-description: Practical data analysis methods and tools across management fields.
916-program-description-2: Starting and managing new ventures, including social enterprises and co-ops, with a major field project and courses from across the Faculty.
917-program-description: Ethics issues in management: social responsibility, transparency, compliance, product safety, data use, UN Sustainable Development Goals, and fair labour.
917-program-description-2: Finance theory, institutions, investment analysis and risk. Leads to careers in finance, government and other firms, up to roles like Treasurer or V.P. Finance.
917-program-description-3: How organizations use IT: the digital economy, choosing and applying technology, and handling data.
918-program-description: Skills for sound management policy across borders. Prepares you for trade, multinationals, banks and government.
918-program-description-2: Employer-employee relations and HR, at the personal level and in their wider context. For more depth, consider the Major.
919-program-description: Skills for policies that support sustainable, responsible development: linked economic, social and ecological challenges, sustainability in business functions, and leading change.
919-complementary-courses-9-credits: 3–9 and 0–6 from two lists, or a related topics course approved by the Mentor and BCom Office.
919-program-description-2: Theory and practice for jobs in product management, advertising, sales, pricing, research, distribution and retail.
920-program-description: Designing and improving processes that make products and services, using quantitative and cross-functional thinking. Careers in consulting, manufacturing, retail, transport, health care and government.
920-program-description-2: Behaviour at work, preparing you for graduate study, general management or HR.
